A cryptographic identity-bonding
 mechanism secures a multi-agent network against Sybil exploitation by forcing nodes to anchor their state into an immutable ledger resembling geological strata, akin to basalt, where each verified node deposits economic stake. This structure absorbs computational erosion like a karst topography, isolating fraudulent nodes before systemic damage occurs. Attackers must continuously burn a verifiable digital pigment representing scarce cryptographic work, making the creation of infinitely scalable fake identities economically non-viable.
